title: Adaptive leaky-bucket provisioning for embeddings endpoint to improve throughput and tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: reduce p95/p99 tail latency and improve stable throughput for embeddings/reranking API under bursty tenant traffic while keeping unit cost within current bounds. Approach: implement an adaptive leaky-bucket admission + predictive scale hint system that decouples request admission from autoscaler decisions. The admission layer enforces tenant-level token buckets with dynamic leak rates derived from active capacity and observed queueing; it exposes a short-lived 'preferred_rate' hint to the autoscaler to shift capacity proactively. This reduces instantaneous queue growth and p99 spikes without overprovisioning. Scope: embeddings.text and embeddings.vector endpoints + rerank pipeline. Excludes persistent model quantization changes.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p99 latency for embeddings endpoint under mixed-tenancy burst test reduced by >=30% compared to baseline (measured on canonical workload)
Sustained throughput (qps) on target cluster improves median throughput by >=15% under bursty arrivals without increasing 99th percentile GPU utilization beyond 5%
No regression in single-tenant steady-state latency (p50/p95) >5%
Autoscaler reacts to 'preferred_rate' hints without oscillation for at least 30 minutes in chaos test
Feature toggle allows immediate fallback to current admission policy and is controllable via Console per-tenant
technical_notes: Admission semantics: per-tenant leaky buckets use a sliding-window leak calculation that takes into account KV cache hit rate and batching efficiency. Leak rate = base_rate * batching_factor * cache_factor where batching_factor is estimated from recent batch sizes.

Predictive hints: small exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) predictor computes a 30s 'preferred_rate' and emits it via the router-event bus and autoscaler API. Autoscaler uses it as a soft target with dampening to avoid oscillation.
Capacity accounting: we add an 'active_headroom' metric per GPU pool which subtracts reserved system headroom and warm-pool capacity from total capacity to compute safe leak ceilings.

Fallback behavior: when the admission layer detects autoscaler lag > 90s, it will gracefully tighten leak rates and reject new requests with a specific 429 reason code 'rate_limit_adaptive' plus suggested retry-after header.

Trade-offs considered: tight admission reduces p99 but increases rejected requests; we favor predictable tail latency for high-SLA tenants and provide opt-in leniency for low-tier tenants. Alternative of immediate overprovisioning rejected due to cost impact.
test_plan: Unit tests for leaky-bucket math, EWMA predictor, and leak-factor calculations
Integration test harness in staging that replays production arrival traces with variable burstiness (low/moderate/high) against current and new admission policies
Chaos tests: kill autoscaler leader and simulate slow scale-up to verify graceful tighten path and 429 semantics
Load test: multi-tenant 100-customer synthetic workload with percentile reporting for p50/p95/p99, GPU util, and rejected requests per minute
A/B rollout canary capturing real traffic with 10% of tenant-traffic for 48 hours and automatic rollback if p99 > baseline*1.15 or reject-rate > 2% for high-tier tenants
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): feature flags and unit tests merged behind 'adaptive_admit_v1' flag. Internal perf runs only
Phase 1 (staging): enable on staging clusters with synthetic workloads. Validate metrics & logs. (owner: Miguel)
Phase 2 (canary): route 10% production requests for non-enterprise tenants for 48h. Monitor p99, reject-rate, autoscaler events. Roll forward to 25% if stable.
Phase 3 (tiered opt-in): expose per-tenant control in Console to opt-in enterprise tenants and allow automatic fallback. Gradually increase coverage to include enterprise tenants if SLA holds.
Phase 4 (ga): enable by default with monitoring alerts and runbook. Document in runbook + postmortem template for regressions

2026-03-03 - Miguel Santos: Implemented leaky-bucket core and local simulator. Observed 35% p99 reduction in synthetic burst replay for 8k qps bursts (staging). PR opened for review.
2026-03-05 - Priya Rao (PM): Prioritizing this to P0 for upcoming sales security review; flagged that enterprise tenants require per-tenant opt-out controls in Console before GA.
2026-03-07 - Engineering review: decided to emit 'preferred_rate' hints rather than hard autoscaler mandates to avoid global oscillation. Added dampening of hint ingestion in autoscaler (factor=0.6).
2026-03-09 - Design feedback (Nate Li): Request small UX addition: surface 'recently guided rate' and reject reason in tenant metrics page. Filed DES-214 for follow-up.

2026-03-10 - QA: Found edge case where predicted batching_factor overestimates when many small requests arrive interleaved with large ones. Added smoothing window and lower bound of 1.0 to batching_factor.
